description: django-oscar has no module-level `urlpatterns` in any of its 828 Python files. Every application is a CLASS; each contributes its routes by overriding `get_urls()`, points each registration at an attribute it resolved from a class NAME in `ready()`, and is served under a prefix a DIFFERENT config composed by mounting it by label. Three facts in three files and not one of them a literal where it is read: 219 declared routes enumerated 30, and 279 functions reading caller input were reachable from nothing. Every positive here is reachable only through that chain and each one is a different link of it -- a view resolved by name from a loader call, a view three mounts deep whose address no single file carries, and a view wrapped in an access decorator at the registration, which is how 33 of oscar's 196 are written. The negatives are the ways the chain does not reach the ground: a `get_urls()` on a Django ModelAdmin, which is the same method name and the same shape mounted by machinery that writes no label anywhere, so its address is not readable; and a view name two modules of this program both define, where binding the route to either would be a claim that a request to that address runs that function and one of the two claims is false. Both negatives carry a live command injection, so a pass that claims either shows up as a finding at an address the application does not serve. The fourth positive is the shape this corpus was kept for: a config-registered FormView, which answers POST through `form_valid` rather than through a method it names -- 28 of oscar's registrations. It used to be a single entry point at ANY on whichever hook came first, so the body that acts on the request was off the surface; then it became two entry points, at GET and POST, carrying no finding at all, because a Django class-based view reaches the request through `self.request` and the taint model sourced a handler's request PARAMETER and route captures and not a property of the view. `self.request.<field>` is a source now on a view a route reaches, and the `cp /tmp/upload <destination>` in `form_valid` is reported at the address and verb the enumeration already had right. The GET half still carries nothing: `get_context_data` reads `self.request.GET` into a template context, and a context is not an interpreter -- which is the difference between a source that fires and a source that is merely loud.

expected.note: reached only through `CatalogueOnlyConfig.get_urls()`, whose view argument is `self.detail_view` -- an attribute assigned in `ready()` from a string naming a class in another package
three configs compose this address: the reviews app is mounted by the catalogue app, which is mounted by the shop, which the root URLconf mounts at the empty prefix
the registration wraps the view in `login_required(...)`, so what is registered sits one call deep inside the argument of another call

the FormView half. `form_valid` takes no request parameter -- Django assigns the request to the view before calling it -- so this body sat on the surface with the right verb and no caller data in it until `self.request` became a source
